So, can you read it to me so it makes sense?

The FCC has net neutrality on its agenda. Net neutrality would prevent internet service providers (ISPs) from throttling bandwidth (and, therefore, internet traffic) to certain servers. There is support to make internet service a utility like water and gas.

Without neutrality, an ISP can lower bandwidth to certain websites' servers. Imagine Voat had information Comcast didn't like, Comcast could throttle the bandwidth to Voat's servers, making it difficult for Comcast users to get that information. You could make a website and ISPs would be able to restrict access to your site.

Overall, the neutrality aspect is to allow equal bandwidth access to all parts of the Internet, so it is contradictory to say they are protecting free speech when they are against net neutrality.
